`insight:forensic-redflag-checklist` | 2026-11-19 | tickers: - | confidence: verified

Distilled from ~30 blow-ups (Satyam, DHFL, IL&FS, Yes Bank, Cox & Kings, Ricoh, Zee, ADAG, Future, Enron, WorldCom, Wirecard, Valeant, GE...). Score each; 3+ hits = do not own without a variant view. CASH: (1) cumulative CFO / cumulative PAT < 0.7 over 5 years; (2) FCF negative for 3+ years while reporting profits; (3) interest income / average cash far below market rates (Satyam fake cash); (4) cash held by third parties/trustees or 'restricted' (Wirecard). WORKING CAPITAL: (5) receivable days or inventory days rising faster than sales for 2+ years (Ricoh, PC Jeweller); (6) working-capital sign contradicts business model (Cox & Kings). CAPITALISATION: (7) capex/sales or capitalised R&D/interest rising vs peers; CWIP aging (WorldCom). RELATED PARTIES: (8) loans/advances/investments to promoter entities, 'general purpose corporate loans' (RHFL); related-party acquisitions (Maytas). GOVERNANCE: (9) auditor resignation, qualified opinion, delayed results (Byju's, Ricoh); (10) independent-director or CFO exits; (11) promoter pledge >25% or rising, falling promoter stake (Zee, Satyam); (12) frequent restructurings/demergers/name changes. BALANCE SHEET: (13) net debt/EBITDA >4x or interest cover <2x outside utilities (IL&FS); (14) short-term funding of long assets. MARKET: (15) rating downgrades/CP-spread spikes; (16) credible short-seller report; (17) insider selling into strength; (18) regulator action on management (Yes Bank). Composite screens: Beneish M > -1.78, Altman Z < 1.81, Piotroski F <= 3 (see separate insights).

**Links:** part_of -> `insight:disqualifiers`, about -> `insight:avoid-ruin`
**Sources:** <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beneish_M-score> ; <https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/rhfl-fund-diversion-case-5-year-market-ban-for-anil-ambani-24-others-124082300983_1.html> ; <https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satyam_scandal>

`theme:sector-specialty-chemicals` · confidence: single-source · tickers: SRF, PIIND, NAVINFLUOR, AARTIIND, DEEPAKNTR, CLEAN, VINATIORGA, UPL

**How it makes money:** Custom synthesis/CSM contracts + specialty intermediates + import substitution; know-how and process cost are the moats.

**Metrics that matter:**
- Volume vs realisation growth
- Gross margin / EBITDA per kg
- EBITDA margin
- Asset turns on new capex
- CWIP and capex commissioning timelines
- CSM order book / # innovator customers
- Working-capital days
- Top-product share

**Value chain and where margins sit:** Crude/feedstock (benzene, toluene, fluorspar) -> basic chemicals -> intermediates -> specialty/AI -> formulator (global agchem/pharma). Margins rise with complexity and regulatory lock-in (CSM, fluoro specialties); commodity intermediates face China pricing.

**Cycle drivers:** China capacity/dumping, global inventory cycles, feedstock prices, trade remedies, monsoon (domestic agchem), innovator patent cliffs.

**Lead indicators (public India data):**
- China chemical price indices / PPI
- DGTR anti-dumping initiations and final findings
- Global agchem majors' channel inventory commentary
- Commerce Ministry export data (organic chemicals HS 29)
- IMD monsoon & kharif sowing data

**What separated winners from losers:** Winners: rising complexity, IP-like processes, customer stickiness, conservative balance sheets through downcycles. Losers: commodity intermediates, single-molecule concentration, debt-funded capex before contracts, aggressive inventory build.

**Valuation ranges and peaks/troughs:** P/E 50–80x at the 2021–early 2022 peak; 25–45x in 2023–25 after destocking. EV/EBITDA 15–35x. Troughs coincide with peak China dumping, which is when P/Es look high on depressed earnings.

**Current state (Nov 2026):** ICRA (31 Aug 2026): domestic-led volume recovery, global overcapacity caps prices. CRISIL: FY27 revenue growth ~6%, margins pressured. Anti-dumping duties on 14 more Chinese chemical categories confirmed in Q1 FY27 (single source). US tariff on Indian agchem 18% vs 35% on China. Mixed Q2 FY27: India Pesticides revenue −21.6%, Sharda Cropchem PAT +23%.

**Classic traps:**
- China+1 extrapolation
- New-capacity revenue never reaching asset-turn guidance
- Inventory gains in rising price markets reported as margin
- Paying peak multiples on peak margins

`person:group-infosys-founders` · flag: **clean** · confidence: verified · tickers: INFY

Flag: CLEAN. Infosys is the reference case for disclosure and minority treatment in Indian IT: founders/promoter group own only ~13%; no pledging; capital-allocation policy returns ~85% of free cash flow over 5 years via dividends and buybacks. Buybacks: 2017 (Rs 13,000 cr), 2019, 2021, 2022 and the Rs 18,000 cr tender at Rs 1,800/share approved 11-Sep-2025, in which the promoters chose not to participate (their stake rising slightly to ~13.4% as shares are extinguished). Governance episodes: (1) 2016-17 founder-board conflict over CEO Vishal Sikka, the Panaya acquisition and severance pay to ex-CFO Rajiv Bansal; Sikka resigned (Aug-2017); Nilekani returned as chairman; an external probe found no wrongdoing in Panaya. (2) Oct-2019 anonymous 'ethical employees' whistleblower letter alleged accounting manipulation by CEO Salil Parekh/CFO; the audit committee's independent probe (with law firm) found no evidence; the US SEC closed its inquiry (2020); stock fell ~16% in a day then recovered -- a whistleblower allegation not upheld. (3) SEBI settled insider-trading proceedings involving some employees (no promoter wrongdoing). Status Nov-2026: no open promoter governance issues; GST demand disputes are tax matters. Investor read: buyback decisions where promoters abstain are a strong signal of alignment.

- **allegations:** 2019 whistleblower (not substantiated)
- **good conduct:** 85% FCF return policy; buybacks; promoters skipped 2025 buyback

body:
```
python3 tools/sec_fetch.py selftest                       # 8 live checks — ALL PASS on 2026-11-20
python3 tools/sec_fetch.py facts AAPL [--quarterly] [--years N] [--csv f] [--raw]
python3 tools/sec_fetch.py concept AAPL us-gaap NetIncomeLoss
python3 tools/sec_fetch.py frames Revenues CY2024 --top 20
python3 tools/sec_fetch.py filings AAPL --form 10-K,10-Q,8-K,"DEF 14A",S-1,4 [--items 4.01,4.02] [--all]
python3 tools/sec_fetch.py doc AAPL <accession> --list | --out f [--file name] [--text]
python3 tools/sec_fetch.py insider AAPL --limit 40 [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--out f.json]
python3 tools/sec_fetch.py holdings13f 1067983 [--accession X] [--top 30]
python3 tools/sec_fetch.py search '"going concern"' --forms 10-K --from 2026-01-01 --to 2026-11-20 [--ciks AAPL] [--page 2]
```

What `facts` covers: it merges fallback XBRL tags for revenue, gross profit, operating income, net
income, diluted EPS, CFO, capex, FCF (derived), SBC, buybacks, dividends, diluted shares, shares
outstanding, cash, long-term debt, equity, goodwill, receivables and inventory. Where a value was
amended, the latest filing wins. It also prints automatic checks: SBC/FCF, CFO/NI, change in
diluted shares, and receivables growth vs revenue growth.

What `insider` covers: it parses the raw Form 4 XML into transaction code, shares, price, value
and the 10b5-1 flag. It sums open-market buys and sells separately from off-plan sells, and it
flags clusters of three or more distinct insiders trading within 30 days.

What `holdings13f` covers: it finds the info-table XML, aggregates by issuer/CUSIP/put-call and
corrects for the units change (thousands of dollars before 2023-01-03, whole dollars after).

Gotchas:
- 10-Q cash flows are year-to-date, so `--quarterly` CFO is mostly blank.
- Fiscal Q4 is not filed as a standalone quarter. Derive it as FY minus 9M.
- Form 4 codes M and A carry a price of 0.

Sample outputs (XBRL as filed):

| | Apple FY to 26-Sep-2026 | Snowflake FY to 31-Jan-2026 |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $478.83B | $4.68B |
| Net income | $132.18B | –$1.33B |
| CFO | $145.10B | $1.22B |
| FCF | $136.06B | $1.12B |
| SBC | $13.79B (10% of FCF) | $1.60B (143% of FCF) |
| Diluted share count, YoY | –1.9% | +1.4% (after $873.5M of buybacks) |

These are single-source figures from SEC XBRL. Cross-check them before using any of them in a report.

`insight:flag-low-early-roce-context` · verified

RULE: a low current ROCE matters less than the ROCE on capital deployed 2-3 years ago (incremental ROCE) and whether today's capital base contains non-earning items. BENIGN WHEN: (1) the denominator holds large CWIP/new capacity not yet earning (Bharti ROCE 3-7% FY18-21 during network build and the price war -> 18% FY26; Apollo Hospitals 7% FY18 with new hospitals ramping -> 17%); (2) the capital base is inflated by investments marked to market or held at cost (Info Edge 2-4% ROCE around a ~58% margin core); (3) EPS is cyclically or one-off depressed (Trent 1% in FY21 -> 31% FY25). REAL WHEN: ROCE stays low after projects are commissioned (Reliance stayed 8-12% for a decade even after Jio matured, which capped returns at ~18% CAGR rather than multibagger rates); when repeated new capex keeps resetting ROCE without the old projects ever earning; when the industry's structure (fragmented, commoditised) prevents high returns at maturity. TEST: (a) ROCE excluding CWIP and non-operating investments; (b) incremental ROCE = change in EBIT / change in capital employed over 3-5 years; (c) segment ROCE for mature units; (d) management's stated payback/ROCE hurdle vs delivered.

body:
- **Screener vs XBRL definitions.** On Q2 FY27 most structured calls agree to within 0.05 pp. Two do not:
  Sona BLW (XBRL OPM 23.04% vs screener 22.53%) and Kaynes (13.18% vs 12.59%). Screener reclassifies some
  items. On the real Q3 data, the disagreement rule sends any such case to review. That matters most for
  SONACOMS, whose threshold is 23.0%.
- **NSE pledge endpoint.** It returned an empty list on 22-Nov-2026, a Sunday. The resolver treats an empty
  answer as transient and retries the next night. INDOTECH is not checked before Apr-2027 anyway.
- **Assisted regexes.** These were tested on Q2/Q3-2026 documents: P&G organic +4% ("four percent") and the
  ICICI Lombard combined ratio. They capture the *first* match, which can be the wrong period. In the
  ICICI Lombard test it caught H1 instead of the quarter. A proposal is never an outcome.
- **The 7 pilot calls (20-Nov-2026).** They have no written resolution rule and no base rate. Their specs
  are taken from their titles, and they are scored for "ours" but left out of skill vs base. Consider
  adding a base rate before they resolve.
- **Possible two-source upgrades.** HUL and Marico (company-reported EBITDA governs) and the bank/NBFC KPIs
  are assisted only. `tools/promise_tracker/pipeline/bank_kpis.py` could move GNPA/NIM checks to
  structured later.
